account: On 14 August 2023 KBAK (Bakersfield) reported a mandatory evacuation for Skyline Drive between Saddleback Drive and Cumberland Road in Bear Valley Springs. It gave an estimated 40 acres, forward progress stopped by 2:17 p.m. and the evacuation lifted by 3:12 p.m. The Kern County Fire Department said that the fire “was started by an electrical strike”. KBAK illustrated its report with photos credited to ALERTCalifornia, but its text does not say how the fire was first reported. A KGET headline the same day blamed lightning and said that no homes were damaged. Cal Fire's archived incident record lists the Trotter Fire at Trotter Drive and Skyline Drive, west of Tehachapi, Kern County. It names the Kern County Fire Department as the agency in charge, so the fire was not a Cal Fire incident. The record gives the start as 11:10 a.m. on 14 August 2023, which is 18:10 in Coordinated Universal Time. The fire burned 52 acres. In universal time the record dates its 100% containment and its extinguishment to 17 August 2023. In local time it gives containment as 5:00 p.m. on 16 August 2023. The record lists the cause as under investigation and says nothing about how the fire was detected or reported. Microsoft made a $5 million contribution to ALERTCalifornia that included a $3 million Azure grant, which ALERTCalifornia announced on 3 February 2026. Since February 2026 Microsoft has worked with ALERTCalifornia's research team through the Microsoft AI for Good Lab. Microsoft's “Unlocked” feature “The first five minutes” (Bruna Mori, 27 August 2026) says that in 2023 ALERTCalifornia's cameras and AI helped crews rapidly detect and contain the Trotter Fire at 52 acres. ALERTCalifornia founder Neal Driscoll estimates that without AI-powered imaging the fire may have spread to nearly 4,000 acres. The feature quotes Zachary Wells, deputy chief of the Kern County Fire Department and deputy director of operations at ALERTCalifornia. The claim of AI detection is found only in Microsoft and ALERTCalifornia material. No fire-agency, regulator or independent news account of the fire mentions AI detection. None says which agency received the alert or when the alert came relative to 911 calls.

Cal Fire's incident record and KBAK's same-day report say nothing about how the fire was detected. KBAK attributes the start to an electrical strike.

fields.account: On 14 August 2023 KBAK (Bakersfield) reported a mandatory evacuation for Skyline Drive between Saddleback Drive and Cumberland Road in Bear Valley Springs. It gave an estimated 40 acres, forward progress stopped by 2:17 p.m. and the evacuation lifted by 3:12 p.m. The Kern County Fire Department said that the fire “was started by an electrical strike”. KBAK illustrated its report with photos credited to ALERTCalifornia, but its text does not say how the fire was first reported. A KGET headline the same day blamed lightning and said that no homes were damaged. Cal Fire's archived incident record lists the Trotter Fire at Trotter Drive and Skyline Drive, west of Tehachapi, Kern County. It names the Kern County Fire Department as the agency in charge, so the fire was not a Cal Fire incident. The record gives the start as 11:10 a.m. on 14 August 2023, which is 18:10 in Coordinated Universal Time. The fire burned 52 acres. In universal time the record dates its 100% containment and its extinguishment to 17 August 2023. In local time it gives containment as 5:00 p.m. on 16 August 2023. The record lists the cause as under investigation and says nothing about how the fire was detected or reported. Microsoft made a $5 million contribution to ALERTCalifornia that included a $3 million Azure grant, which ALERTCalifornia announced on 3 February 2026. Since February 2026 Microsoft has worked with ALERTCalifornia's research team through the Microsoft AI for Good Lab. Microsoft's “Unlocked” feature “The first five minutes” (Bruna Mori, 27 August 2026) says that in 2023 ALERTCalifornia's cameras and AI helped crews rapidly detect and contain the Trotter Fire at 52 acres. ALERTCalifornia founder Neal Driscoll estimates that without AI-powered imaging the fire may have spread to nearly 4,000 acres. The feature quotes Zachary Wells, deputy chief of the Kern County Fire Department and deputy director of operations at ALERTCalifornia. The claim of AI detection is found only in Microsoft and ALERTCalifornia material. No fire-agency, regulator or independent news account of the fire mentions AI detection. None says which agency received the alert or when the alert came relative to 911 calls.

purpose: Built to detect smoke in camera feeds and alert fire agencies. The claimed detection is that purpose.

ratings.reason: The fire was held to 52 acres and the evacuation lifted the same afternoon (Cal Fire record; KBAK), a risk removed for the neighborhood. The claim that the camera network detected it first comes only from ALERTCalifornia's founder via Microsoft.
